content:
Proctor, Vermont's Wilson Castle combines 19th-century charm with tales of paranormal activity

Inside the Wilson Castle in Proctor, Vermont, visitors get full tours offering both history and paranormal intrigue.

PROCTOR, Vt. —

Wilson Castle in Proctor, Vermont, is a historic mansion that offers visitors a glimpse into 19th-century life while carrying a reputation for paranormal activity.

"It's a Gilded Age mansion. The castle is built for a holistic medicine healer and is very, very rich. New York City socialite way. Unfortunately, they didn't last here very long. They only lived in the house for eight years," said Douglass "Andy" Probst of Wilson Castle.

The mansion changed ownership several times before Herbert Lee Wilson purchased it in 1939 for $12,000.

"He was a radio engineer. He was responsible for building, fixing and installing radio stations, installing transmission lines all over the world. He did work on the Vatican's radio station. He did work for Vermont Radio," Probst said.

The Wilson family owned the castle until 2009. Today, it has become a destination for paranormal enthusiasts.

"The rumbling started in the '70s. Guests would actually pull the various tour guides aside to say that they'd seen a lady looking out the windows in the upstairs bedroom with a sense of sadness and a heaviness upstairs. And the tour guides were told honestly by the Wilsons not to discuss anything of the sort," Probst said.

Probst added that the spirits are believed to be welcoming rather than wicked.

"It's believed that the prior owners, the Johnsons, are here, and then some members of the Wilson family as well," he said.

Visitors are encouraged to keep their eyes and ears open during tours, as guides say you never know what you might encounter while walking through the house.

"The transport casket typically is on the third floor," Probst said. "This thing has been used many, many times by the local funeral home. And it was used to transport dead bodies."

Probst noted that the second floor is where most paranormal activity is reported.

"Sarah's room has always had the reputation of being the most active since the '70s. You would be reported looking out the windows. They did determine that the Johnsons lost their firstborn son. So the thought is, is that Sarah's mourning the loss of that child," he said.

Probst added, "The running joke here is, if you're kind to Sarah, she'll leave the heat on for you."

The castle's haunting stories attract tourists, paranormal investigators and artists hoping to capture its beauty — and perhaps something unexpected.

"This is a very unique opportunity to be able to freely walk around, take your time and, you know, see what your eye catches you," said photographer Nick Lehman.

Proceeds from visits help fund restoration projects to preserve the castle, which are supported by the local community.

For those who prefer history over hauntings, Wilson Castle offers tours from Memorial Day through Halloween, showcasing this unique piece of Vermont's past.
